profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record sits at 1005 West Geneva Drive in Tempe, Arizona, within the Phoenix metropolitan area, tagged as a data center under the name Omnis Network. The name combines a common Latin derived business prefix with a direct reference to networking, a pattern often used by small internet service providers, managed network companies, or hosting operations, which would make a modest network services facility at this address plausible. A company called Omnis does have a public web presence, but it belongs to an unrelated software business based in the United Kingdom that develops cross platform application development tools, with no mention of Arizona, Tempe, or any physical network or data center facility. That company appears to be a coincidental name match rather than the operator of this Tempe address. No other website, business filing, or press coverage specific to Omnis Network at this location could be identified. Because the most obvious lead turned out to belong to a different, unrelated company, this entry does not attempt to describe Omnis Network's actual business in detail. It is published as an honest record of what is and is not confirmed about the Tempe facility, and will be revisited if a verifiable local operator is identified.
profile.research_note: Address 1005 West Geneva Drive, Tempe AZ 85282, confirmed via reverse geocode and OSM tags. omnis.net resolves but is an unrelated UK-based cross-platform app development company (Omnis Software), no Arizona or data center connection, a coincidental name match only. No AZ-specific Omnis Network domain could be reached. Cannot confirm operator.

reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap-tagged data center in Tempe, Arizona has no published power, floor space, or IT capacity, and its operator cannot be confirmed.

The record places a facility at 1005 West Geneva Drive in the Phoenix metro area under the name Omnis Network. The only company reachable under that name is a UK software developer with no Arizona or data center connection, which the research treats as a coincidental match. No press coverage, business filing, or operator website specific to this address was found. The entry is documented rather than characterized.

Arizona has 57 mapped data center facilities, and only four of them publish power figures, totaling 512 MW. This location is not among those four. That gap is the point for AI infrastructure: a mapped building is not a measured load, and the state's published capacity reflects a small minority of its sites. Power and IT specifications are what would let anyone place a facility in the compute stack, and here they do not exist.

What this does not tell you is whether the site is a large campus or a small colocation closet, whether it is active, or who runs it. It also does not establish that the tag is correct. The absence of published specifications is not evidence of small size, only of missing data.
